title: Meta Stock Falls 2.0% After United Bans AI Agents (Nov 11)
summary: META fell 1.97% to $628.77 on Nov 11 as The Wall Street Journal tied the drop to United Airlines blocking AI assistants from booking tickets.
body_markdown:
Large-cap peers were split.[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) rose 2.11%, Nvidia gained 2.87% and Apple added 2.04%, while[Microsoft (MSFT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/msft/) fell 2.26% and[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) lost 1.74%. Meta closed 19.37% below its 52-week high of $779.82 and 20.86% above its 52-week low of $520.26.


## Why Meta Stock Fell


According to[The Wall Street Journal](https://finance.yahoo.com/m/72271530-a9c2-3f34-bdbc-d83774c1cc0d/meta-stock-slips-after-united.html) , Meta shares fell about 2% after the paper reported that United Airlines plans to block personal AI assistants from the systems it uses for booking tickets.


As reported by[One Mile at a Time](https://onemileatatime.com/news/united-airlines-bans-ai-agents-protect-customers/) , United updated its contract of carriage to prohibit "the use of AI Agents to make, modify or service a Ticket, and/or to purchase any service or product." The airline's definition explicitly covers AI assistants built into social media or search platforms, AI-enabled browsers and third-party assistants that connect through travel agencies. In a release, United said, "Sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information."


Meta also had company news during the session. According to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/meta-infrastructure-departure-aws-cloud.html) , Santosh Janardhan, Meta's head of infrastructure, wrote in an internal memo that "it's time to pass the baton" to David Brown, a former AWS senior vice president who joined Meta in July. Janardhan will leave in 2027 after supporting Brown through the first quarter. The report did not link the announcement to the share move.


## META Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- The infrastructure handover is planned: Brown will lead Meta's infrastructure work under the Meta Compute initiative, and Janardhan will stay through the first quarter of 2027 to support him, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/meta-infrastructure-departure-aws-cloud.html) .
- The data center tax risk is a scenario, not legislation.[TIKR](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/democrats-could-target-data-center-201808689.html) notes that Democrats have not formally proposed ending 100% expensing, and that a cut would spread deductions over future years rather than remove them.


### Risks


- United's rule reaches AI assistants built into social media and search platforms, and the airline said it will restrict that access both on its own platforms and through travel agencies and aggregators, per One Mile at a Time.
- Spending remains heavy. CNBC reports that Meta expects full-year capital expenditure of $135 billion to $145 billion, logged negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, and saw S&P Global Ratings change its outlook on the company from stable to negative in late October.
- Democrats, set to control both chambers of Congress in January after the November 3 midterms, could seek to end 100% expensing for data center equipment, according to Baird Strategas' Daniel Clifton as cited by TIKR. TIKR adds that Meta has no third-party cloud business, which may leave it more exposed than Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon.
